cells.tense: Something is arriving toward you now and you're already inside it, choosing it, with your hand on the pen today.
cells.ask: Write down one connection you already said yes to — not why, not how it's going, just that you chose it. One line. Naming what you've gathered keeps it yours.
cells.core:
You meet what shows up as it is. A conversation starts and you stay in it; someone comes toward you and you don't step back. That exchange is happening often enough that you can feel it working — there's something here that wasn't here before, and you're the one who agreed to it.

What makes it yours is that you can say so. You don't have to explain the choice or defend it or rehearse why it's right. You write one line saying you took it, and that line holds your place in it. What you gather this way keeps going, because you're standing on it rather than hovering over it.
cells.sheetLine: You're in it now, and you're the one who chose to be.

cells.tense: You're already at a future that hasn't happened, planning the end of a connection that's still beginning.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that's still forming and leave it undecided today — don't refine the plan, don't rehearse the conversation. See whether the ground holds without your grip. That's what tending without forcing gives back: room to find out.
cells.core:
Picture a week where you meet people exactly as they arrive. Someone says something and you answer it; a collaboration builds itself one exchange at a time. You're not arranging the outcome, you're just present with what's actually here — and a result that grew because you let it has a weight the arranged version doesn't.

But you're meeting them in advance. You've run the scene six ways before it starts, and the run-through is doing the connecting instead of the real moment. What's distorted is the timing. You're trying to write the ending before the middle has happened. Loosening the grip on one thing isn't surrender — it's the care that doesn't exhaust itself.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing a connection before it's had a chance to arrive.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, still holding the handle.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about a connection you haven't said yet — to a notebook or a voice memo, plain words, for no one else. What you see lands clean without arguing.
cells.core:
Something arrives and you reach back; someone knocks and you answer while they're still there. That's how it goes when the door is open, and it's not complicated — the door stays open, the answer comes at the time it's needed.

But the door has closed, and it closed at your end. Something that was arriving got met with a delay — not a refusal, a wait — and the wait became the posture. You're not short on the ability to connect. You're short on the moment when it was actually available, and now it's in the past. What you already see is still there. The door is what needs attention.
cells.sheetLine: The door opened and you were still deciding.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but this is already being written — the page is full and you're calling it blank.
cells.ask: Look at one connection you're in and say out loud who made the first move. Just once, just to yourself. Claiming the direction already running through your life.
cells.core:
You notice your own part in what's arriving. You see the moment you reached first, the sentence you offered that opened something, the call you made before anyone else did — and you can hold it without making it a big deal. That noticing is steady and quiet, and it keeps the connection yours instead of something that happened to you.

It starts before you clock it. A connection forms, something clicks, and you describe it as if it just happened — as if the meeting were the tide. But someone chose it. You were there for that choice. You keep handing the credit to the situation instead of to yourself, and then you wonder why the direction feels like it isn't yours. Point at one thing you started and say you started it. Direction comes back that way — not by doing more, but by seeing what you were already doing.
cells.sheetLine: You've already started this. You're just not claiming it.

attempts.check: No cell names what the connection is, who it is with, or what was chosen; the card's own face is decisive connection, and every cell stays at the level of what this capacity is doing now. A reader might say the Too Little cell assumes a specific door was refused; the tense line keeps that as a location in time and the ask never requires them to find or reopen it. The asks survive being wrong: naming one thing without asking anything back and clearing the ground around one choice each teach something even if the read misses, and the Too Much ask does not require a partner to be present. The sentence that flatters the writer most is 'you don't wait for the proof to settle' in Balanced — it is doing the work the tense line already did; it stays only because the rest of the core earns it, and the Unacknowledged cells are the ones to watch for the same move.
